criteria.requirement: Exhaustive health states render with explicit warning tone and words.
Calendar-aware freshness distinguishes stale, paused, never-run and failure.
Bounded history queries and typed diagnostics preserve useful cause without secret or personal data.

Safe retention, retry and tombstone behavior survive a disposable real restore.
Standard OAuth PKCE connection and refresh preserve selected authority.
Revocation, downgrade, token replay and metadata SSRF attacks are refused.
Existing login and account isolation remain intact; auth secrets excluded from recovery.
Direct SDK transport can discover and call safe diagnostic tools with consistent guards.
Bounded result handles isolate callers and recheck revoked authority.
Compatible server upgrade preserves connection; catalog budget and schema-version errors are tested.
Preview and actual execution enforce current delegation, target versions and optional approval.
Concurrent replay, target conflict, budget reservation and fenced workers produce one authorized effect.
Crash and uncertain provider results reconcile without blind duplicate execution; readback is honest.
Repair cases preserve source issue, expected result and sanitized evidence.
Foreign/fabricated engineering evidence is rejected; PR, merge, deploy and verification stay separate.
Issue resolution follows actual verification and preserves rollback/domain restrictions.
Signed-in reporters submit and track private bug or improvement reports without cross-account access.
Screenshot/context pipeline strips sensitive metadata and enforces safe upload authorization and limits.
AI opt-in, withdrawal, privacy export/deletion and restore suppression cover all report content.
Agent tools enforce support scopes, report AI permission and internal/reporter separation.
Reports support private conversation, duplicate/case links, evidence-backed resolution and reporter reopen.
Prompt injection and withdrawn consent cannot authorize new actions or leak derived private content.
Stored schedules, leases, cursors, cooldown and outbox survive restart and overlapping workers.
Owner-selected delegation permits supported actions and revocation stops queued execution.
Heartbeat and external-worker status are truthful; notification retry does not duplicate or recurse.
Bounded aggregate observations carry baseline, sample and provenance without sensitive dimensions.
Improvement proposals include verification, risk and rollback without silently executing changes.
All in-scope maintenance/settings controls have tested tools or a genuine provider-required handoff.
RTC doors conform to pinned upstream contract and use the same native authorization as direct MCP.

Read-back on both apps afterwards: POST /api/mcp without credentials returns 401 with the OAuth challenge, and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp and /api/auth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server answer with that app's issuer and endpoints; the public storefront still returns 200.

Consent-fix landing and trial re-run 2026-11-02 (owner-ordered): PR #835 merged at head 67125e64 (squash c9e7e882 on main) after a genuine pull_request CI cycle at that exact head (run 41582580558, success on the guarded re-run of its one failed browser shard) and the review-gate's waived self-review success at the same head, 0 unresolved threads. The testing branch was synced to c9e7e882 and the dedicated testing app redeployed from it; its health endpoint read back revision c9e7e8822a47b9a115e857ae0c4fab230502f244 (the production app was not deployed). The acceptance trial was then re-run end to end against that revision (full record in the Official MCP SDK client row): registration, synthetic-owner sign-in, the authorize-to-consent redirect and the consent page all pass, but submitting Allow still fails with the app's error page and records no connection. A second, independent defect in the same step is now proven as the blocker: the consent page drops the authorize query's repeated ba_param entries — the provider's own signed-parameter list — when it re-serializes the query into the approval form, so the provider refuses the consent call with 400 invalid_signature. The #835 Origin repair is confirmed necessary and correct (with the complete query, no Origin still earns the 403 refusal and Origin earns 200 with an authorization code issued), but it is not sufficient while the page mangles the signed query. The client row stays NOT_PROVEN, A3 stays PARTIAL and MCP-9 stays IN_PROGRESS; first reads, refresh and the disconnect proof sit behind consent and stay unproven.

evidence: 2026-11-02, dedicated testing app at that revision: a real client (public PKCE client 'Vivienne MCP-9 trial (Official MCP SDK)') was registered through the live dynamic-registration endpoint, and its authorize request reaches the app's sign-in (302 to /login carrying the signed OAuth parameters). Authenticated initialize/whoami/read NOT_PROVEN — waiting on the testing owner's sign-in and consent (owner checklist).

Real-client trial attempt 2026-11-02 (runbook docs/runbooks/MCP-9-CLIENT-ACCEPTANCE.md, dedicated testing app at ed78f50d, health endpoint read-back of the same revision): the official SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0; trial harness 'MCP-9 trial (Official MCP SDK)') was driven through live dynamic registration (public PKCE client, token auth method none), the synthetic testing owner signed in through the app's sign-in API (200, OWNER), authorize redirected to the consent page (302), and approval through the consent API plus the token exchange were observed directly (200, Bearer, 600 s, scopes ops:read and decisions:read plus the standard offline_access refresh permission; a refresh token was issued). The trial is blocked by a proven app-side defect in the consent page's Allow action (src/app/connect/consent/actions.ts): the action calls the OAuth provider through auth.handler with a hand-built request that carries the session cookie but no Origin or Referer header, and in production the provider's CSRF origin check refuses exactly that shape before the consent handler runs. Proof, all live on the testing app: (1) the owner reproduced the failure in a real browser session (2026-11-02 19:00-19:03 MST) — the consent page rendered correctly for his client and tapping Allow, twice, produced the app's error page; (2) programmatic submissions of the action (both standard form protocols, page-exact values, fresh clients) returned HTTP 500 and recorded no connection (System health read-back: no connection listed for the trial client); (3) an A/B call on the consent endpoint with the same session and signed query — cookie-only with no Origin: 403 (code MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN); with Origin set to the app's own address added: 200 and an authorization code. No test catches this because the provider library skips the origin check under NODE_ENV=test (isTest default in @better-auth/core context creation) and the app never overrides it, so the loopback round-trip suite runs with the check off. A token issued without the connection record the action was supposed to write carries no connection-version claim and POST /api/mcp refuses it ('Assistant authorization is required'), verified with the SDK client. whoami, the scoped read, refresh-and-repeat and the revocation proof therefore remain NOT_PROVEN. The smallest fix — carry the app's own issuer Origin on that server-to-self call, with a regression test pinning the request shape — is ready in PR #835, deliberately unmerged for the owner's word; after it merges and the testing app redeploys on the nightly route, this trial re-runs. Nothing in this row is marked PASSED.

Trial re-run 2026-11-02 against the dedicated testing app at revision c9e7e8822a47b9a115e857ae0c4fab230502f244 (PR #835's consent Origin fix, deployed to the testing app only and read back from its health endpoint): live dynamic registration (201, public PKCE client, token auth method none — the registration validator requires application_type native for a loopback callback, noted for future harnesses), the synthetic testing owner signed in through the app's sign-in API (200, OWNER), authorize redirected to the consent page (302) and the page rendered the client name and the two read scopes (ops:read, decisions:read, plus the offline_access refresh permission). Submitting the page's own Allow action with the page's rendered values (both standard form protocols, fresh clients) returned HTTP 500 and recorded no connection (the assistants page still read 'No assistants connected yet'). Root cause proven by a local reproduction of the exact production build (same tree c9e7e882, production mode, throwaway database — the server log shows the action's 'expired or was rejected' throw) plus a four-cell A/B replay against the provider's consent endpoint: (a) the query exactly as the consent page submits it — src/app/connect/consent/page.tsx re-serializes the authorize parameters keeping only single-valued ones, dropping every repeated ba_param entry — is refused 400 {"error":"invalid_signature"} with and without an Origin header; (b) the complete authorize query is refused 403 MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN without Origin (the original defect) and returns 200 with an authorization code when the #835 Origin header is present. The Origin repair is therefore real and required, and the page's query re-serialization is a second, independent defect in the same step: until the page carries the complete signed query through to the action, Allow cannot succeed for any client, browser or harness. First scoped reads (initialize/whoami/read), token refresh and the disconnect proof remain NOT_PROVEN — they sit behind the consent step, and a token issued without the app-level connection record is refused by the assistant door (proven in the previous attempt).
Owner decision 2026-11-02: the assistant connection is an owner-only tool; no hub connection will be made or tried. This row is closed by that ruling, not by a trial.
